headline: Generative models probe complexity and identifiability limits in evolutionary dynamics
label: Models Of Evolutionary Dynamics
summary: Recent preprints and a published SSE analysis test when evolutionary models generate complexity and what their outputs can identify.
synthesis: The dominant thread is the use of explicitly defined models to ask when evolutionary dynamics produce structure and when inferences about those dynamics are supported. Hash Chemistry extends a minimal model with spatial locality and GPU simulation, reporting that space size controls a transition in open-ended evolutionary dynamics. Causal emergence measures applied to the GARD catalytic model indicate that causal organization precedes and promotes molecular self-replication. On the inferential side, a published analysis shows that SSE diversification models are unidentifiable through hidden states, and that false-positive inferences arise from model proliferation across congruence classes. The food-web backbone and siderophore network studies apply structural inference to empirical data across 129 mammal food webs and nine bacterial taxa, though their abstracts do not report identifiability analyses. What is new is the pairing of generative simulation with formal limits on what model outputs can identify.
